messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Thompson <ben.thompson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Acme TCO post-call recap / next steps

Hi Ben  great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps.

1) Pain points you shared
- Token spend is the single largest line item across our LLM experiments (esp. higher for embedding + chat flows).
- Sporadic spikes in traffic create big monthly variance and upset the forecasted budget.
- Current latency targets are 200ms p95 for production flows; some of your heavy-batched reporting calls are much higher.

2) Goals we discussed
- Reduce effective per-request cost by ~30-40% while keeping p95 latency under 200ms for interactive flows.
- Predictable monthly bill (budget within +/- 10%).
- Maintain accuracy/quality on search & summarization tasks.

3) Cost/TCO levers we flagged
- Token economics: identify high-token prompts and refactor or truncate; estimate tokens-per-call distribution.
- Batching & concurrency: group low-latency-safe requests for throughput endpoints to lower per-token cost.
- KV / prefix caching: cache repeated prefixes for chat sessions to avoid re-sending context.
- Quantization / model variant routing: use a cheaper quantized variant for background jobs and a higher-quality model for front-line UX.
- Dedicated vs hosted: reserved capacity for predictable workloads to stabilize unit pricing.

4) Immediate requests / next steps
- From you: sample prompt set (5-10 representative queries), expected monthly QPS and peak QPS, and a rough monthly budget target.
- From us: we'll produce a back-of-envelope token-volume estimate and a TCO worksheet (attached) showing 3 scenarios: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved, and mixed routing + caching.

I attached a short worksheet (acme_tco_worksheet.xlsx) with the three scenarios  I filled in some assumptions based on what you said. Rafael and I can run the numbers together once you share the prompt samples and traffic profile.

Thanks  talk soon.


Marissa Cole

Thanks Ben  that budget context is super helpful. Quick ballpark math based on the ~70M production tokens: 

- Baseline hosted (current): if avg cost is $0.0008 per token -> ~$56k/mo (shows why noisy eval traffic is inflating spend).
- With simple batching + prefix caching: expected ~25-30% reduction -> ~$39-42k/mo.
- With optimized routing (quantized background model for non-critical flows) + reserved capacity on steady-state -> could get to mid-$20k range depending on commit level.

Key assumptions I used (in the attached redwood_tco_quickmath.pdf): average tokens per request = 350, 70M tokens monthly production, batching effective for 45% of requests, caching reduces re-sent tokens by ~30% on chat-heavy flows. We'll refine these once we see prompt samples and a little telemetry.

For anonymization: sample prompts + per-request token counts + timing (qps) is enough. No PII needed. If you can strip user identifiers and return timestamps relative to start-of-day, that works. If helpful we can send a short script that redacts PII while preserving token counts.

Next proposed meeting: 30-min technical dive to review prompt mix + run a quick profiling pass. Rafael  are you available tomorrow at 11am PT?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: redwood_tco_quickmath.pdf (calculation summary)
